stem_book: The sphere at A is given a downward velocity v₀ of magnitude 5 m/s and swings in a vertical plane at the end of a rope of length l = 2 m attached to a support at O. Determine the angle θ at which the rope will break, knowing that it can withstand a maximum tension equal to twice the weight of the sphere. (Figure: OA horizontal; θ is the angle of the rope below the horizontal OA.) (Take g = 10 m/s².)
reason: stem: stated g = 10 m/s² - the key sin⁻¹(1/4) needs it
work: v² = 25 + 2g·l sinθ; T = mv²/l + mg sinθ = m(12.5 + 30 sinθ) = 2mg = 20m ⇒ sinθ = 1/4 (g = 10, not printed)
